get.description: Returns the failsafe channels and missing temp-source references currently tracked by the daemon.

200.description:
Full current health snapshot returned by `GET /devices/health`.

 Two sections with different meanings, deliberately not interleaved.
 `failsafe`, `missing`, `stale_source` and `firmware_overrides` are
 **current state**: conditions that can clear on their own.
 `channel_capabilities` and `system_findings` are **permanent**: facts about
 what this hardware can do, which will not change while the machine is
 running. Presenting a permanent capability as a fault would imply the user
 should wait for it to resolve; presenting a fault as a capability would
 imply the opposite.

get.description: Returns running min/max/avg/count per channel and temp since daemon start. Entries are present once observed at least once.

200.description:
Top-level response for `GET /stats` and `DELETE /stats`. One entry per
 known device. Channels/temps are only present once they have been
 observed at least once since daemon start (or last reset).

delete.description: Clears all running stats and reseeds each from the most recent status with count=1. Channels absent from the most recent status are dropped and will reseed naturally on their next observation.

post.description: Runs each device duty through the calibration's stable inverse and returns the true duties that reproduce it, in the same order. A calibrated channel reinterprets stored duties as true-duty, so a curve authored before calibration behaves differently; feeding its points through here yields values that restore the old behavior. Rejects an empty list, more than 256 entries, or any duty over 100.

phase.description: One of: queued, running, done, failed, cancelled.

CalibrationBatchStatus.description:
Status of the single active calibration batch. The batch driver owns
 each entry's `phase`, so the UI renders progress straight from this
 without disambiguating a fan's sticky prior calibration. The running
 entry carries live `percent`/`stage` lifted from its per-channel
 status; a failed entry carries the `message`.

CalibrationEntryView.description:
Same wire shape as `crate::calibration::CalibrationEntry`, with
 the wrapped view in place of the bare calibration.

CalibrationOverridesUpdate.description:
Per-fan calibration override values. `null` clears the override
 and falls back to the auto-derived behavior (heuristic for the
 boost, calibrated `kick_duration_ms` for the duration, walk-down
 enabled by default).

CalibrationStatus.description:
Per-channel status of the latest calibration attempt. The UI polls
 `GET /calibrations/.../status` to drive its progress UI; the engine
 rewrites this entry on every sweep step and once more on the final
 terminal transition. The `Completed` and `Failed` variants stick
 around until the next diagnosis on the same channel resets it back
 to `InProgress`. `NotStarted` is returned when neither an in-memory
 snapshot nor a persisted calibration exists for the channel; the
 endpoint returns 200 in that case so the UI does not have to
 distinguish "channel unknown" from network errors via HTTP 404.

CalibrationView.description:
Calibration as exposed via the REST API. Flattens the persistence
 struct and adds derived fields the UI consumes.

down_curve.description: Down-sweep samples. Same shape, dense around the kick-in zone.

kick_boost_active.description:
Resolved kick-boost decision (override + heuristic). `true`
 when the dispatcher will apply the cold-start boost on the
 next Off->Kicking transition for this channel. Derived; the
 deserialize path is only used for JSON round-trips in tests
 and will be recomputed if `kick_boost_override` changes.

kick_boost_override.description:
User override for the cold-start kick boost. `None` defers to
 the heuristic (`needs_kick_boost`); `Some(true)` forces the
 boost on; `Some(false)` forces it off.

kick_duration_ms.description:
Measured time from writing `min_start_duty` to RPM crossing the
 start floor, plus a 50% safety margin. Used by the dispatcher's
 Off -> Kicking -> On hand-off. Bounded by the daemon's poll rate
 so values land on second-aligned increments.

kick_duration_override_ms.description:
User override for the kick-write duration. `None` uses the
 calibrated `kick_duration_ms`; `Some(ms)` forces the dispatcher
 to hold the kick for `ms` before dropping to sustain. Useful
 when a fan needs longer than the measured start-to-spin time to
 stabilize at the boosted kick duty.

max_eff_duty.description:
"Near plateau" duty (within `jitter` of `rpm_max`). Informational:
 `true_to_device(100)` can still write above this on fans that
 keep gaining RPM past it.

min_stable_duty.description:
Lowest device-duty without oscillation. Equals `min_sustain_duty`
 on healthy fans; sits above it on firmware-kicked fans that
 oscillate just above sustain (dispatcher clamps kick + sustain
 to this value).

min_start_duty.description: Lowest device-duty that reliably starts the fan from rest.

min_sustain_duty.description: Lowest device-duty that keeps the fan spinning once started.

up_curve.description: Up-sweep samples (duty 0..=100 ascending). Dense in kick-in, sparse above.

walk_after_kick_override.description:
User override for the post-kick walk-down. `None` defers to the
 default (walk down in small steps from kick to sustain); `Some(true)`
 forces the walk on; `Some(false)` jumps from kick straight to
 sustain. Skipping the walk is safe on hardware that tolerates an
 abrupt drop and removes a visible 1-22 second ramp on every cold
 start. Serialized with `#[serde(default)]` so calibrations written
 before this field existed deserialize cleanly to `None`.

warnings.description: Non-fatal reliability findings. Empty for a healthy calibration.

CalibrationWarning.description:
Non-fatal reliability findings. The calibration persists either way;
 these inform the popover and the completion notification.

oneOf.description:
Tachometer reported 0 RPM throughout: fan disconnected, tach
 wire unplugged, or firmware holding the fan off.

Fan spins but does not track duty (RPM span within noise). Most
 often BIOS/firmware-controlled. Mapping disabled (forced Stepped).

Usable RPM span is small enough that mapping resolution is coarse.
 Mapping stays active.

Fan never settled above `min_sustain_duty` (cheap firmware-kicked
 fan). `min_stable_duty` undefined; dispatcher falls back to
 `min_sustain_duty`. The range marks the observed oscillation band.

Derived model leaves nothing to map: a duty floor high enough that
 every duty the map can write is already max speed, or a responsive
 region that never rises. Both come from unreliable RPM reads
 during the sweep. Mapping disabled (forced Stepped).

CalibrationsDto.description:
Snapshot of every persisted calibration. Empty list when nothing
 is stored. Matches the wrapper shape used by `/profiles` and
 `/alerts` so clients can iterate `dto.calibrations`.

ChannelAssignment.description:
A fan-to-profile assignment the run proposes. `replaces_profile_name` is set when the
 channel already has a non-default profile that Create & Apply would replace, so the UI
 can warn the user before overwriting it.

ChannelEvidence.description:
The raw facts a `ChannelVerdict` was computed from.

 Carried alongside the verdict so every surface can show what was measured
 rather than asking the user to trust a label.

 The bools are four genuinely independent sysfs observations, not a state
 machine that wants an enum: any combination of them can occur on real
 hardware, and collapsing them would discard the evidence this type exists
 to carry.

has_pwm_enable.description:
A missing `pwmN_enable` is not a defect. Drivers implement different
 feature sets; its absence usually means only that fan control cannot be
 handed back to the BIOS. It is evidence *against* `FirmwareOverride`,
 because there is no auto mode to revert to.

ChannelExtensionNames.description:
Channel extension names that signal which `ChannelExtensions` are applicable
 for a particular device channel.

ChannelExtensions.description:
Device Channel specific settings
 This is used to store specialized settings (extensions) that apply to a specific device channel.

anyOf.description: Whether to use the device channel's internal hardware fan curve functionality.

Whether to use the AMDGPU RDNA3/4 features.
 It allows the device to run at zero RPM when the temperature is below a certain threshold.

hw_fan_curve_enabled.description:
Whether to use the internal HW Curve feature, instead of setting regular
 flat curves. Using this reduces functionality.

label.description: The channel display label. A null or absent value removes the override.

ChannelOverrides.description: A table per channel so color/ignore/compute can slot in later.

channel_label.description:
Daemon-written detected-label hint for hand-editors and rename
 dialogs, ignored on read (never a resolution layer).

ChannelSource.description:
A source for displaying sensor data that is related to a particular channel.
 This is like `TempSource` but not limited to temperature sensors. (Load, Duty, etc.)

channel_name.description: The internal name for this channel source. NOT the Label.

device_uid.description: The associated device uid containing current values

ChannelStats.description:
Running min/max/avg/count for a single (channel, `data_type`) or temp pair.
 `count == 0` means no observation yet; min/max/avg are unused in that state.

ChannelVerdict.description:
Why a fan channel can or cannot be driven, from local evidence only.

 `FirmwareOverride`, `IgnoresDuty` and `Unverifiable` can only come from a
 duty-response probe, which is not part of this work. They stay in the
 taxonomy and in the wire shape so the probe can land later without moving
 the API; until then nothing produces them, which is the honest answer.

oneOf.description: `pwmN` is present and writable and nothing has reclaimed it.
Manual mode was set and later read back as something else.
No writable control, on a family where an out-of-tree driver may help.

The driver in use exposes no control for this channel. Reported by
 repositories that know only whether a channel is drivable, with no
 sysfs-level facts to back a more specific verdict.
The driver exposes no `pwmN` for this channel.
`pwmN` exists but the driver cleared its write bit.
Probe proved writes are accepted and the fan never responded.
No usable tachometer, so no probe can settle the question.

ChannelVerdictRef.description: A diagnosis bound to the channel it describes, for the health snapshot.

allow_unencrypted.description: Allow unencrypted HTTP connections from non-localhost addresses

device_listener_enabled.description: Whether to listen for device add/remove events at startup

origins.description: Custom origins to allow in CORS (for reverse proxy setups)

protocol_header.description: Header to check for proxy client protocol (e.g., "X-Forwarded-Proto")

sensors_auto_detect.description: Whether to auto-detect Super-I/O sensors at startup (`x86_64` only)

sensors_conf_enabled.description: Whether to apply labels and ignores from the lm-sensors configuration

CustomSensor.description:
Variant-specific payload of a `CustomSensor`, internally tagged on `cs_type`. Exactly one
 variant is valid per sensor. Constraints the type cannot express (single source for
 `Offset`/`TimeAverage`/`ExponentialMovingAvg`, `offset` in `-100..=100`,
 `time_window_seconds` in `1..=300`) are enforced at the API boundary in
 `validate_custom_sensor`.

children.description:
The Custom Sensor's children, if any.

 Each Custom Sensor is either a child, parent, or standalone, not a combination of those.
 Custom Sensors are limited to 1 level of hierarchy. This removes the possibility
 of circular references.

 The children and parents vectors are managed and filled internally. For GET endpoints,
 they provide this information for clients. For POST or PUT endpoints,
 any values here are essentially ignored.

id.description: ID MUST be unique, as `temp_name` must be unique.

parents.description: The Custom Sensor's parents, if any. See `children` for more details.

DesktopNotification.description:
A desktop notification event broadcast to connected clients via SSE.
 The daemon decides when to notify; clients decide how to display.

probed.description:
False when no probe was made at all, so an empty `detected_chips` means
 "not looked for" rather than "none present". Detection can be switched
 off by config or environment, and is unsupported off `x86_64`.

device_id.description:
The chip's own id register. Reported so a chip line in a pasted report
 can be matched against a pasted log.

DeviceExtensions.description:
Device specific extension settings
 This is used to store specialized settings (extensions) that apply to a specific device.
 More than one of these settings can be applied at a time.

delay_millis.description:
The delay in milliseconds to force between applying settings to this device.
 This is to help with communication issues with some devices that may not handle
 multiple settings applied in quick succession. (The driver does not always handle this)

direct_access.description:
Whether to enable Direct Access for the liquidctl driver,
 which will cause liquidctl to ignore the `HWMon` kernel driver

DeviceHealthDto.description:
Full current health snapshot returned by `GET /devices/health`.

 Two sections with different meanings, deliberately not interleaved.
 `failsafe`, `missing`, `stale_source` and `firmware_overrides` are
 **current state**: conditions that can clear on their own.
 `channel_capabilities` and `system_findings` are **permanent**: facts about
 what this hardware can do, which will not change while the machine is
 running. Presenting a permanent capability as a fault would imply the user
 should wait for it to resolve; presenting a fault as a capability would
 imply the opposite.

channel_capabilities.description:
Permanent: channels that cannot be driven, and why. Controllable
 channels are omitted; there is nothing to report about working hardware.

firmware_overrides.description: Current state: firmware reclaimed a channel this daemon controls.

system_findings.description:
Permanent: machine-scope facts, such as a detected chip with no driver
 bound or a probe blocked by the environment.

unreachable.description: Current state: devices whose driver has stopped answering entirely.

amd_gpu_overdrive.description:
When present, then this is an AMD RDNA3/4 GPU with PMFW fan curve support.
 True indicates overdrive is enabled and fan control is available.
 False indicates overdrive needs to be enabled via kernel boot parameter.

temp_max.description: The absolute maximum temp to use for Profiles for this device

temp_min.description: The absolute minimum temp to use for Profiles for this device

thinkpad_fan_control.description:
When present, then this is a `ThinkPad` device. True or False indicates whether Fan control
 is enabled for the kernel module and changing values is possible

name.description: The device display name. A null or absent value removes the override.

channels.description: Temps and channels share one namespace, keyed by raw channel name.

device_name.description: Daemon-written hint for hand-editors, ignored on read.

name.description: User override for the device display name.

status_history.description: Status history wrapped in Arc for O(1) cloning for serialization

locations.description:
If available various paths used to access the device.
 This can include paths like the kernel device path, hwmon path, HID path, or PCI Bus ID

name.description: If available the kernel driver name or liquidctl driver class.

version.description:
If available the driver's version.
 For kernel-based drivers this is the current kernel version.
 For liquidctl-based drivers this is the liquidctl version.
 For Nvidia-based drivers this is the version of the installed nvidia proprietary drivers.

DriverType.description: The Driver Type, or source of the driver actively being used for this device.

DutySample.description: A (device-duty, RPM) sample. Curves are sorted ascending by `duty`.

EnvironmentBlocker.description: Why the Super-I/O probe could not run.

FailsafeDelta.description: SSE delta broadcast when a channel/temp enters or leaves failsafe.

reason.description:
Why the node entered failsafe, matching the transition log line (for
 example "stale readings" or "file unreadable"). Fixed at entry, so a
 latched node never produces reason-only transitions.

FailsafeKind.description:
Whether a failsafing node is a temp or a control channel. One entry per node
 (a fan is a single `Channel`, not separate rpm/duty entries).

FailsafeRef.description: A present channel/temp currently serving failsafe values.

reason.description:
Why the node entered failsafe, matching the transition log line (for
 example "stale readings" or "file unreadable"). Fixed at entry, so a
 latched node never produces reason-only transitions.

FanAssignment.description:
One fan the user has assigned a cooling role to. Fans the user skips are omitted from
 the request entirely.

laptop_temp_strategy.description: Laptop temp strategy, honored only when `kind` is `LaptopFan`.

position.description: Case-fan mounting position, used only to name the generated profile.

FanKind.description:
The cooling role a fan plays. Assigned explicitly by the user: fan roles cannot be
 reliably auto-detected (an AIO pump can be wired to an ordinary motherboard fan header),
 so a wrong guess is worse than none.

FanPosition.description:
A case-fan mounting position. Label only: it affects generated profile names, never the
 generated curve.

Function.description:
The function type discriminator (`f_type`) and the fields valid for that type. Most `Function`
 fields (the step-size/hysteresis and safety-latch config) apply to every type and stay on
 `Function`; only these are type-specific. Per-variant fields stay `Option` so requiredness is left
 to apply-time validation, keeping the input wire contract backward-compatible.

bypass_min_at_extremes.description:
Whether to bypass the minimum step size when the target duty is exactly 0% or 100%.
 Useful for ensuring fans fully stop or reach max RPM even when the change is below the
 minimum step size. The maximum step size is still respected. Disabled by default.

duty_maximum.description:
The maximum duty change (step size) to apply
 A duty maximum of `0` indicates a fixed step size. Use `duty_minimum` to set the step size.
 Previously `duty_maximum`.

duty_minimum.description:
The minimum duty change (step size) to apply
 Previously `duty_minimum`.

name.description: The user given name for this function

step_size_max_decreasing.description:
The maximum step size to apply when decreasing.
 A value of `0` indicates a fixed step size. Use `step_size_minimum_decreasing` to set the step size.

step_size_min_decreasing.description:
The minimum step size to apply when decreasing.
 A value of `0` indicates a symmetric step size. Use `duty_minimum` to set the step size.

threshold_hopping.description: Whether to temporarily bypass thresholds when fan speed remains unchanged for 30+ seconds to meet curve target.

uid.description: The Unique identifier for this function

deviance.description: The temperature deviance threshold in degrees

only_downward.description: Whether to apply settings only on the way down

GenerateProfilesRequest.description: The full input to one profile-generation run.

GenerateProfilesResponse.description:
The proposed result of a generation run. Nothing here is persisted; the UI previews it
 and the user confirms before the existing create endpoints persist it.

discrete.description:
Discrete GPUs are listed first and are what a stress test normally
 means to target.

id.description:
Opaque selection key to pass back as `gpu_id`. The PCI slot where one
 is known, e.g. "0000:03:00.0".

name.description: Driver-reported name, e.g. "AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (RADV NAVI22)".

HealthEntityType.description: The kind of config entity that holds a temp-source reference.

KeyTemps.description:
The canonical system temps the user has identified, pre-filled by the UI but verified by
 the user. Each is optional because not every system exposes all of them (no dGPU,
 air-cooled, no ambient probe). A CPU temp is the minimum needed to generate anything.

LaptopTempStrategy.description:
Which temperature a laptop fan should follow. Honored only when the fan's kind is
 `LaptopFan`.

oneOf.description: An EMA custom sensor wrapping the real CPU temp. Sensible default for most laptops.
The `ThinkPad` CPU temp sensor read directly.
A Mix(CPU, GPU) using the Max function, so a disabled dGPU reading 0C is ignored.

driver_type.description: An Enum representation of the various Liquidctl driver classes

firmware_version.description: The detected firmware version at initialization

unknown_asetek.description: An indicator for needed user input to determine actual asetek690lc device

LcdCarouselSettings.description:
Settings for the LCD Carousel.

 This can be used to have a carousel of images (static or gif), of sensor data,
 or a combination of both.

images_path.description:
The absolute path directory location for images for the carousel. All applicable images
 present are processed when the setting is applied.

interval.description: The interval in seconds (2-900) in which to change images in the carousel.

gif_supported.description:
Whether this screen can show an animated gif. The Kraken 2023 on firmware 2.x
 cannot, and liquidctl refuses outright, so the mode has to stop offering it.

LcdSettings.description:
LCD mode and its mode-specific fields, internally tagged on the `mode` discriminator
 (lowercase, as before). Named `LcdModeKind` to avoid colliding with `device::LcdMode`, the
 device-capability struct. The per-mode fields stay `Option` for now: the enum already makes
 a mode structurally unable to carry another mode's field; requiredness is still enforced by
 the existing apply-time validation.

orientation.description: The LCD orientation (0, 90, 180, 270). Applies across modes, so it stays shared.

colors.description: a list of RGB tuple values, eg [(20,20,120), (0,0,255)]

MapDutiesRequest.description:
Body for the duty map. Device duties as authored before the channel
 was calibrated.

MapDutiesResponse.description: True duties, one per request entry, in the same order.

NotificationIcon.description:
Icon types for desktop notifications.
 Each variant maps to a specific icon image displayed in the notification.
 Serialized as `snake_case` strings for SSE consumers (Qt app, web UI).

modes.description:
Power profile name to Mode UID. Profiles left out are unmapped and are ignored when the
 system switches to them.

PowerProfileSnapshot.description: A point-in-time view of the power profile integration, for API consumers.

active.description: The profile currently in effect, if one has been observed.

available.description:
Profiles the system daemon offers. Empty when no power profile daemon has been reached,
 which is how a client knows to hide the feature.

modes.description: Profile name to Mode UID. Profiles absent here are deliberately unmapped.

Preset.description: The noise/performance tradeoff applied to a generated profile.

PresetOverride.description:
A per-kind preset that overrides the global preset for one kind. Case intake and exhaust
 are coupled (they share one base Mix profile), so both must carry the same preset; that
 is enforced at the generation boundary, not by the type.

function_uid.description: The function uid to apply to this profile.

speed_fixed.description: The fixed duty speed to set. eg: 20 (%)

speed_profile.description: The profile temp/duty speeds to set. eg: [(20.0, 50), (25.7, 80)]

offset_profile.description:
The graph offset to apply to the associated member profile. Can also be a static
 offset when there is only one duty/offset pair.

full.description: Include the whole hwmon tree instead of the compact summary.

report.description: The report as plain text, ready to paste.

Setting.description:
Setting is used to store applied Settings to a device channel.
 These are the general core settings that apply to a wide range of device and channel types.
 Specialized settings are stored in `DeviceExtensions` and `ChannelExtensions`.
 Only one specific lighting or speed setting is applied to a specific channel at a time.

 The kind of setting is enforced at the type level via `SettingKind`. The serialized
 shape is preserved (flat fields under the channel object) for backwards compatibility
 with both the persisted TOML config and existing REST clients.

anyOf.description: Apply a fixed duty speed to the channel. eg: 20 (%)
Apply the named profile to the channel.
Apply lighting settings to the channel.
Apply LCD settings to the channel.

SourceDelta.description: SSE delta broadcast when a missing reference appears or resolves.

channel_name.description: The channel the setting is on. Only set for LCD references.

entity_name.description: Display name: profile/device name, or the sensor id.

entity_uid.description: Profile uid, Custom Sensor id, or the owning device uid for an LCD setting.

source_device_name.description:
Name of the device owning the missing temp, resolved from the live
 device set or the config `devices` list (gone devices stay listed).

A config reference whose temp-source target is absent from the current device
 set. The `entity_*` fields let a client badge and deep-link to the owning
 editor; `source` is the referenced {`device_uid`, `temp_name`}.

channel_name.description: The channel the setting is on. Only set for LCD references.

entity_name.description: Display name: profile/device name, or the sensor id.

entity_uid.description: Profile uid, Custom Sensor id, or the owning device uid for an LCD setting.

source_device_name.description:
Name of the device owning the missing temp, resolved from the live
 device set or the config `devices` list (gone devices stay listed).

SourceStateDto.description: The wire-visible state of one watched source.

extension.description: If present, then this channel has special settings that are applicable.

fixed_enabled.description: True if manual fan speed control is supported; if false, speeds are read-only (monitoring only).

max_duty.description: The maximum fan duty for this speed channel

min_duty.description: The minimum fan duty for this speed channel

SseEvent.description:
Every event `/sse` publishes, pairing the SSE event name with its payload.

 This is the single source of truth for the wire format. Substreams construct these
 and `Event::from` is the only place an event is named, so the compiler rejects a new
 variant until it has a name and a payload. The `OpenAPI` schema derives from the same
 type, which is what keeps the documentation from drifting away from what is sent.

 The serde representation models a frame logically as `{"event": ..., "data": ...}`.
 The wire form is SSE framing (`event: status\ndata: {...}`), not that envelope:
 `OpenAPI` 3.1 has no way to describe a stream of tagged frames, so the envelope is the
 closest honest description. `sse_event_names_match_serde_tags` pins the two together.

oneOf.description: One poll tick of every device's most recent status.
Temp sources that appeared or disappeared this tick.
Temp sources that went stale or recovered this tick.
Channels that entered or left failsafe this tick.
Devices that stopped or resumed answering this tick.
Full device-health snapshot, sent to a consumer that lagged the transitions.
One or more daemon log lines, pre-coalesced. Raw text, not JSON.
The mode that just became active.
An alert whose state changed.
A desktop notification for the client to display.
A change in observed system state, discriminated by its `kind`.

events.description: Comma-separated substreams to subscribe to. All of them when absent.

StartCalibrationBatchRequest.description:
Body for `POST /calibrations/batch/start`. `concurrency` is how many
 sweeps run at once (1 = sequential); omitted or 0 is treated as 1, and
 the daemon clamps it to the channel count.

backend.description:
Which backend to use. Omit for the daemon's default
 (stress-ng if installed, else built-in).

duration_secs.description: Duration in seconds. Defaults to 60, max 600.

thread_count.description: Number of threads. Defaults to all available CPU cores.

backend.description: Which backend to use. Omit for the daemon's default (built-in).

duration_secs.description: Duration in seconds. Defaults to 60, max 600.

threads.description: Number of I/O threads. Defaults to 4.

backend.description: Which backend to use. Omit for the daemon's default (built-in).

duration_secs.description: Duration in seconds. Defaults to 60, max 600.

gpu_id.description:
Which GPU to stress, as an `id` from GET /stress-test/gpus.
 Omit to stress every GPU.

backend.description:
Which backend to use. Omit for the daemon's default
 (stress-ng if installed, else built-in).

duration_secs.description: Duration in seconds. Defaults to 60, max 600.

StatsResponse.description:
Top-level response for `GET /stats` and `DELETE /stats`. One entry per
 known device. Channels/temps are only present once they have been
 observed at least once since daemon start (or last reset).

Status.description: A Model which contains various applicable device statuses

StressBackend.description: Which backend is running (or will run) a stress test.

SystemEvent.description:
A change in observed system state, broadcast to connected clients via SSE.

 The daemon reports what changed; clients decide what to do about it. `previous` is `None` for
 the first observation after the daemon connects to the source.

SystemEventKind.description:
What kind of system state the event describes.

 This exists so external consumers can subscribe to one stream and dispatch on `kind` rather
 than needing a new event name, and a new SSE substream, per integration.

oneOf.description: The system power profile, as reported by `power-profiles-daemon` or `tuned-ppd`.

SystemFinding.description: A fact about the machine rather than about one channel.

oneOf.description: A chip was detected but no loaded driver serves its family.
modprobe refused because the driver is blacklisted.
The probe could not run at all.

Not an `x86_64` target, so no probe was ever attempted. Distinct from
 `BlockedByEnvironment` because the stub reports `has_dev_port: false`
 on platforms where `/dev/port` is simply irrelevant, and reporting that
 as a blocker would be a claim we cannot back with an observation.

device_uid.description: The associated device uid containing current temp values

temp_name.description: The internal name for this Temperature Source. NOT the `TempInfo` Label.

UnreachableDelta.description: SSE delta broadcast when a device stops or resumes answering.

consecutive_timeouts.description: Consecutive operations that timed out before the device was given up on.

UnreachableRef.description:
A device whose driver has stopped answering, so the daemon can neither read from it nor write
 to it.

 Distinct from `FailsafeRef`, which means the device is alive with stale readings and safe
 values substituted. Presenting this as that would tell the user their fans are on a safe curve
 when no curve can be applied.

consecutive_timeouts.description: Consecutive operations that timed out before the device was given up on.
